alex.chen: Hey team — quick onboarding question. I got my onboarding packet and a physical reimbursement card in the mail. Does the recurring $100/month home office stipend hit that card or payroll? I tried activating the card and the site shows `pending verification`.
people-ops: Congrats and welcome! The one-time welcome/reimbursement card is separate from the monthly home-office stipend. The $100/month is normally processed through payroll as a taxable allowance unless you opted into the card payout option on the stipend form. If the card shows `pending verification`, can you confirm if you completed the ID check link in the card activation email?
alex.chen: I clicked the activation link and uploaded a selfie + ID photo yesterday. No error messages, just the pending state. If payroll handles it, when would the first payment land? Second pay period?
jamie-m: For context — the monthly stipend runs on the 15th of each month after the first full month following your start date, unless you chose the card. For payroll method it's on the regular payroll deposit (labelled "HomeOfficeStipend" on the stub). If you started mid-month, the first payout may be prorated.
people-ops: @alex.chen — we can check card activation status on our side. DM us your last 4 of SSN or employee ID and we'll look up the verification flag. If the card provider still needs docs, they usually email with the missing item.
alex.chen: Sent you a DM with my emp id. Also — does this affect health benefits effective date? My start date was Mar 16. I enrolled within the 30-day window but the MyBenefits portal shows "effective date pending".
people-ops: Good question. Medical/dental effective dates are typically the 1st of the month after 30 days for hires in the middle of a month. Because you started Mar 16, your medical/dental would kick in on May 1 in the standard flow. However if you enrolled and selected the expedited option on the enrollment form, we can sometimes backdate to Apr 1 — check the enrollment confirmation email for "expedite request accepted".
alex.chen: Ok that makes sense. Anything I need to upload for dependents or HSA to speed things up?
people-ops: If you enrolled dependents, please upload proof of dependent (birth certificate or marriage certificate) to the MyBenefits portal within 30 days to avoid delays. For HSA: if you elected company HSA contributions, no extra docs required, just confirm your bank account for HSA transfers in the benefits portal.
lili-r: FYI payroll queue note — prorated stipend and first-month PTO accrual both show up on the first paystub as separate line items (PTOPR and HME_STIP). If you don't see them by the 2nd pay run after start, ping payroll-bot. :slightly_smiling_face:
payroll-bot: Payrun scheduled: 2026-03-31. If you expect a prorated stipend and it doesn't appear, file an inquiry via the payroll help form and reference ticket #auto.
alex.chen: Thanks all — I'll wait for the people-ops DM update and keep an eye on my paystub and the card activation email. One more thing — for expense reimbursements (desk chair, monitor), do I use the physical card or submit expenses?
people-ops: Submit eligible receipts to Expensify under the "HomeOffice" policy for reimbursement. The welcome card is meant for one-off vendor purchases we preloaded sometimes; use it only if the vendor accepts the card and the purchase fits the welcome supply list. Otherwise, expense the receipt and select "HomeOffice Equipment". Reimbursements typically process within 7–10 business days after approval.
alex.chen: Great — that's clear. Appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
